articles.title: 'If Mac Allister's performances are good, he will get a new contract'
articles.summary: Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock said Alexis Mac Allister just needed to be put into a system that suits him to get the best out of him.  "I don't t...
articles.body:
Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock said Alexis Mac Allister just needed to be put into a system that suits him to get the best out of him.

"I don't think he has to show his importance to Liverpool, I think everyone knows the qualities he has got anyway," said Warnock, who was a pundit on Wednesday's Champions League Match of the Day.

"There will be a lot of talk about him because of what has gone on in the past few days, but Liverpool fans were already asking why hasn't he been offered a new contract when other players have.

"To come out and talk about a contract situation like he did, a couple of days before a game, and to be able to back it up the way he did with a good performance is important - but it is over the course of the season where his performances are important. If he wants a contract and he thinks he deserves a contract, then if his performances are good, he will get one.

"We all know the qualities that he has got - he is a World Cup winner, a Premier League winner - it is just that he has got to be put into the right system to make it work.

"At the moment, Liverpool's system is a little bit dysfunctional, but it is starting to get better and he will get better because of that."

articles.title: Champions Seahawks beat Patriots in season opener
articles.summary: Defending champions the Seattle Seahawks come from behind to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 in the opening game of the NFL season.
articles.body:
Defending champions the Seattle Seahawks came from behind to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 in the opening game of the NFL season.

For the first time in 10 years the season began with a rematch of the Super Bowl, in which the Patriots were dominated by a Seahawks defence known as 'the Dark Side'.

Again they stepped up after Seattle lost quarterback Sam Darnold to a hip injury in the game's opening drive, claiming three interceptions in the final quarter at Lumen Field.

The Patriots went into a 10-0 lead, with rookie tight end Eli Raridon scoring the first touchdown of the season in the second quarter.

Back-up quarterback Drew Lock got the Seattle offence going late in the third quarter, with Jason Myers cutting the gap with a field goal.

Seahawks cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett claimed his first career interception at the start of the fourth quarter, after a Drake Maye pass was deflected by rookie Rodney Thomas.

On the next possession Lock found wide reciever Jaxon Smith-Njigba in space and last season's offensive player of the year charged through the Patriots defence for a 45-yard touchdown.

Julian Love then picked off Patriots quarterback Maye, giving Myers the chance to edge the Seahawks in front with a 26-yard field goal.

New England were well within field-goal range with 21 seconds remaining, but chose to go for the win rather than settle for overtime, and the move backfired as Maye's hopeful pass towards Mack Hollins was intercepted by Josh Jobe in the end zone.

The only game in which Maye threw multiple interceptions last season was the Super Bowl, and he was picked off on the Patriots' final three possessions in the season opener.

Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald said initial tests showed Darnold had not fractured a hip.

Week one continues with the NFL's first regular-season game in Australia. The Los Angeles Rams meet the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne on Thursday (01:35 BST, Friday).

articles.title: Qatar beat Iran in men’s basketball as Asian Games begin in Japan
articles.summary: The continental games will officially open on September 19, but several team competitions will get under way earlier.
articles.body:
The Asian Games have begun in Japan with Qatar beating Iran in men’s basketball, the first action in the continental multisport showpiece that has more participants than the Olympics.

Qatar held off a comeback from Iran to win their Group B encounter 59-35 at the Aichi International Arena in Nagoya on Thursday.

It was the first match of a men’s basketball competition that will have medal finals on September 20, the day after the opening ceremony.

“We know we need to win at least one game so we can qualify for the next round,” said Qatar’s Michael Lewis, the United States-born player who scored a game-high 21 points.

“Feels good to get some team camaraderie back, and now we have got to keep going.”

Later in Group B, Taiwan beat Jordan 83-80.

More than 17,000 athletes and officials are expected to take part in 43 sports at the Nagoya-Aichi Games, which do not officially start until the opening ceremony on September 19 and will run until October 4.

Several events such as basketball, football, cricket, hockey and modern pentathlon will get under way before the opening ceremony.

Los Angeles 2028 Olympics qualifying spots are up for grabs in several sports at the Asian Games, which are returning to Japan for the first time since 1994.

Organisers hope the athletes will have a “unique experience” staying in accommodation ranging from a cruise liner and wooden containers to standard hotel rooms.

Officials are confident that the plan will not be affected by Japan’s typhoon season, which is usually in full swing in September-October.

Weather has already caused disruptions, with record rainfall two days ago forcing hundreds of athletes briefly to evacuate their accommodation.

Rainwater also leaked into some competition venues, with more wet weather forecast for the coming days.

Among those in action at the Games will be Philippine tennis sensation Alexandra Eala and a pair of world-class teenage talents: 15-year-old Indian cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and 13-year-old Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi.

articles.title: Former NHL player, coach and longtime ESPN analyst Barry Melrose dead at 70
articles.summary: Barry Melrose's wife confirmed his death at 70 to ESPN, two years after his Parkinson's disease diagnosis forced his retirement from broadcasting.
articles.body: Barry Melrose, the former player and coach who led the Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final before becoming one of hockey’s most recognizable voices in broadcasting, has died. He was 70. ESPN announced Melrose’s death Wednesday after his wife notified Steve Lacy, a former ESPN colleague. Melrose was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease in 2023, prompting his retirement from the network. He joined ESPN in 1996 and spent nearly three decades with the network. "For decades, Barry Melrose was one of the most distinctive and trusted voices in hockey," the network said in a statement. "His knowledge of the game was deep, his candor was refreshing, and his passion was unmistakable. He was a foundational part of ESPN's hockey coverage, and fans and teammates truly appreciated his entertaining delivery and charismatic personality." BILL RASMUSSEN, ESPN FOUNDER WHO CONCEIVED A CABLE NETWORK DEVOTED TO SPORTS, DEAD AT 93 "We send our deepest condolences to his loved ones. He always kept it interesting and he will be missed." Melrose stepped away from sports broadcasting in 2008 for a brief return to coaching, serving as head coach of the Tampa Bay Lightning for 16 games. Melrose compiled an 84-108-29 record as an NHL head coach. Melrose had a relatable everyman’s broadcasting style, bringing a sense of humor to his insights, and was easily recognized by his goatee and slicked-backed hair. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "From the flowing locks of his distinctive mullet to the flared lapels of his trademark long suit coats, Barry Melrose cut an unmistakable figure whenever you were fortunate enough to run into him at a rink or catch him on your television screen," NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman said in a statement. "You were even more fortunate if you engaged him in conversation or listened to his analysis because he never failed to boost your love of the game of hockey." "Barry was my best friend at ESPN," John Buccigross, a longtime colleague of Melrose’s at the network, wrote on social media Wednesday. "A big brother figure of rock solid values. I am shook to my core. Barry gave his life to hockey and some of his ESPN family, like me, learned of his shocking death today while at a hockey rink in Las Vegas preparing for the upcoming season. Chilling and fitting -- the rink was Barry's home. A more beloved ESPN institution there has not been. We love you, Barry. Forever." NEW DETAILS EMERGE SURROUNDING FOUR-TIME STANLEY CUP WINNER CLAUDE LEMIEUX'S DEATH From rural Kelvington, Saskatchewan, Melrose began his professional hockey career with the Cincinnati Stingers of the now-defunct World Hockey Association in 1976. He played three seasons in Cincinnati, the final one alongside a young Mark Messier, before making the jump to the NHL with Winnipeg in 1979 after the WHA folded. Melrose went on to play for Toronto and Detroit, where he closed his career following the 1985-86 season. He finished with 10 goals and 33 points and 728 penalty minutes in 300 career NHL regular-season games, and he skated in seven more in the playoffs. His WHA totals were five goals and 32 points and 343 penalty minutes in 178 games with Cincinnati. articles.title: Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva stripped of neutral athlete status
articles.summary: Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva will not be able to compete internationally after the sport's governing body revokes her neutral athlete status.
articles.body:
Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva will not be able to compete internationally after the sport's governing body revoked her neutral athlete status.

The 20-year-old returned to the ice in January after serving a four-year doping ban but remained ineligible for this year's Milan-Cortina Olympics.

Russian athletes have been barred from competing under their national flag since the country's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, although International Skating Union rules allow for Russians to compete as neutral athletes.

According to those rules, an individual is presumed eligible unless the ISU determines they are in active military/security service for Russia or Belarus, have taken part in military operations against Ukraine or have "publicly supported that war".

The ISU initially granted Valieva neutral status for the 2026-27 season but that has now been refused.

A video featuring Russian president Vladimir Putin is pinned on Valieva's Instagram account.

Russian men's skater Mark Kondratiuk, a team-mate of Valieva's at the 2022 Winter Olympics, has also had his status revoked.

Valieva was 15 when she helped Russia win team gold in Beijing, becoming the first female skater to land a quadruple jump during the Olympics.

But shortly afterwards it emerged that she had tested positive for heart medication trimetazidine - classed as a performance-enhancing drug - six weeks earlier.

A Russian Anti-Doping Agency (Rusada) investigation concluded Valieva bore "no fault or negligence" for the violation, but the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) upheld an appeal by the World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada).

Valieva and her team-mates were stripped of gold, with her ban backdated to when she tested positive in December 2021.

articles.title: Way-Too-Early 2027 Hart Memorial Trophy Rankings for NHL MVP
articles.summary: A slight breeze is in the air, training camp rosters are set and a new NHL season is just around the corner.
articles.body:
A slight breeze is in the air, training camp rosters are set and a new NHL season is just around the corner.

This was an offseason equal parts dramatic and quiet. Some of the biggest stars in the league like Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin have requested trades away from their career-long teams, and yet radio silence has followed these requests.

Big names up for extensions such as Cale Makar and Macklin Celebrini broke NHL payday records which was exciting in itself, but the free market in general was lackluster as most of these big names ended up staying with their original teams.

As the season gets closer, we're starting to envisage the possibilities for star players all around the league.

Let's kick things off with our first Hart Trophy rankings of the 2026-27 season.

Cale Makar's record-setting eight-year, $163.2 million extension reflects his standing among the NHL's elite defensemen.

The 27-year-old has been one of the league's premier blue-liners throughout his seven NHL seasons and has won the Norris Trophy twice.

After signing the extension last month, Makar enters the final season of his current contract with Colorado positioned to contend for another Stanley Cup.

We'll do the obvious disclaimer: Defensemen winning the Hart is extremely rare. Chris Pronger was the last to do it in 2000, when Makar was one year old.

Makar also has the best "problem" in the world working against him: Nathan MacKinnon happens to be his teammate. It's tough to win most valuable player on your team with MacKinnon in the fold.

Still, with the evolution of the defenseman position, more are at least popping up on Hart ballots these days. Makar has already reached 90 points twice, and he's got a Conn Smythe to his name.

He would probably have to outperform MacKinnon, but the thought of Makar making a Hart Trophy splash this season doesn't feel totally unreasonable.

Once Mitch Marner adjusted to life as a Golden Knight last season, there was no turning back.

He enjoyed a historic postseason breakout, leading the entire league in scoring with 29 points in 22 games. He scored a natural hat trick in Game 3 of the SCF, and it was the fastest playoff hat trick in finals history at six minutes and 10 seconds.

Where will Marner go from here? Without Pavel Dorofeyev in the fold, Vegas' top dogs will have to contribute even more.

With a year of acclimation and a stellar postseason under his belt, Marner could make some noise in the Hart Trophy race next season.

The only thing worse for a player's Hart Trophy hopes than Nathan MacKinnon as a teammate? Connor McDavid as a teammate.

Despite playing alongside Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl has previously won the Hart Trophy. If the Oilers are to return to the Stanley Cup Final this season, they will likely need him to approach his peak form again.

Draisaitl has scored more than 100 points in four of his last five NHL seasons, with last season a "down year" featuring 97 points due to injury. If he can remain healthy, he knows the role he has to play in such a monumental year for the Oilers.

Trades That Could Happen Before Training Camp

7. Connor Hellebuyck, Winnipeg Jets (For Now)

It's looking like Connor Hellebuyck will not end up on the Jets by the end of the season, as he requested a trade a few weeks ago.

No matter where he ends up, the official trade request was a gutsy move. Hellebuyck is betting on himself after years of disappointing playoff losses in Winnipeg gave way to a signature performance in Team USA's Olympic win.

While it's rare for a goalie to win the Hart, Hellebuyck did it two seasons ago. He's only one season removed from that historic regular-season performance, and he's got some big-game catharsis after his Olympic run.

Add in a new team with more support around the net, and there's a good chance Hellebuyck reenters the Hart conversation.

Is this the year everything truly comes together for the Wild? They've got some questions to answer, no doubt: There's the Quinn Hughes extension that's yet to be signed, and there's that pesky lingering need for a true first-line center.

Beyond these problems for the front office to solve, the expectation is that star winger Kirill Kaprizov will make the jump to the 50 goal, 100-plus point mark. He eclipsed 100 points in 2021-22 with 47 goals and 108 points in his healthiest season logging 81 games.

He came close to returning to that form last season, recording 45 goals and 89 points in 78 games. With Quinn Hughes set to quarterback the power play for a full season and Matt Boldy continuing his breakout, Kaprizov has the supporting cast to reach those marks again.

GM Bill Guerin's got some work to do if the Wild as a whole are to take the next step, but if Kaprizov does his job he'll put them in a good spot -- and he'll put himself back into the Hart conversation.

Nick Suzuki had been a great, classic-type center since entering the league, but the way he's improved all aspects of his game each season has truly been a sight to behold.

He snagged the Selke last season, and ended ranked fifth in the Hart race as he captained the Canadiens to the ECF. In the process, he became just the third player in NHL history to win the Selke Trophy and score 100 or more points in the same season.

Meanwhile, Suzuki is just 27 and the team around him is bursting at the seams with even younger talent. The Hart Trophy competition is stiff as ever, but it's only up from here for Suzuki and the Habs.

Every year we wonder if we've seen the last of Nikita Kucherov's underrated skill, and every year we are wrong.

The reigning Hart Trophy winner is 33 years old and hungry for more as he and his Lightning refuse to fade into the darkness.

Kucherov remains one of the NHL's most dynamic offensive players, combining elite playmaking with a consistently dangerous shot. That blend of creativity and finishing makes him a centerpiece of the Tampa Bay attack.

He only seems to be getting better with age, scoring over 100 points in each of his last four seasons, with a career-high 44 goals and career-high +43 rating last season to boot.

Again, people get picky when it comes to Kucherov. But does it really matter if you're scoring points on the power play or at even strength if the points keep being scored and the games keep being won? Exactly.

Largely regarded as one of the most complete and competitive players in the game, Nathan MacKinnon has finished as a Hart finalist in five of his past nine seasons, winning the award in 2023-24.

He prides himself on a health and fitness regimen that has helped extend his prime and enabled him to miss just five games over the past three seasons.

The Avalanche had an incredible regular season last year in which MacKinnon led the league in goals, but it ended on a bitter note as the Golden Knights swept them in the Conference Finals.

With Makar's extension and the "now-or-never" state of the franchise, MacKinnon is going to be extra motivated to lift this core to one more Cup.

Macklin Celebrini's sophomore season was a revelation in so many ways. The Sharks center exceeded our very high expectations, jumping from 25 goals, 63 points, and a -31 rating in year one to 45 goals, 115 points, and a +8 rating in year two.

He led the Sharks into the playoff conversation ahead of schedule, even if they ultimately fell short. The then-19-year-old was a standout on Team Canada at the Olympics, which was extra impressive considering Canada's veteran presence.

In his first taste of the biggest stage, he lead the entire tournament in goals with five and came in just behind McDavid in overall points with 10 in six games.

Celebrini is already a bona fide star, and his ceiling remains extraordinarily high. A first playoff berth would mark the next step in his development, giving him a chance to show how far he can take the ascending Sharks in his third NHL season.

If there is any year Connor McDavid would like to reprise his recurring role of "Hart Trophy winner," this would be the one.

The best hockey player in the world is entering the final year of his contract as the Oilers look to turn two unsuccessful Stanley Cup Final appearances into a third trip—and, perhaps, their long-awaited breakthrough.

McDavid finished second to Kucherov in last season's Hart Trophy voting despite leading the NHL in scoring while Draisaitl missed significant time. The result could reflect the depth of Kucherov's case, rather than any perceived voter fatigue.

In any event, McDavid's got three Harts, five Ted Lindsay awards, and zero Cups to his name headed into his 12th NHL season. That last number is clearly the most important to him, but on an offensively weaker Oilers team, he'll probably have to win his fourth Hart on the way to his first Cup.

articles.title: La crono decisiva, desde dentro: programa especial de Radio MARCA

articles.summary: Vicente Ortega dirige de 15:00 a 19:00 horas un programa especial desde El Puerto de Santa María, con Radio MARCA desplegada también en la meta de Jerez de la Frontera
articles.body: Radio MARCA vive este jueves desde dentro una de las jornadas decisivas de La Vuelta. Con motivo de la 18ª etapa, la contrarreloj entre El Puerto de Santa María y Jerez de la Frontera, la radio del deporte realiza un gran despliegue para contar todo lo que suceda desde la salida hasta la meta. Desde las 15:00 y hasta las 19:00 horas, Vicente Ortega dirige un programa especial desde la Real Plaza de Toros de El Puerto de Santa María, punto desde el que toman la salida los corredores. Una emisión realizada con la colaboración de la Diputación de Cádiz y el Ayuntamiento de El Puerto de Santa María, con toda la última hora, protagonistas y análisis de una contrarreloj que puede resultar determinante para decidir La Vuelta. El despliegue permitirá vivir la etapa desde sus dos puntos fundamentales. Radio MARCA estará en la salida de El Puerto de Santa María y también en la meta de Jerez de la Frontera, siguiendo todo lo que ocurra antes, durante y después de la contrarreloj. José Rodríguez pondrá voz a la carrera, siguiendo en directo los tiempos, las referencias intermedias y las diferencias entre los grandes favoritos. Cada segundo puede ser decisivo en una jornada llamada a marcar la clasificación general. Por el programa pasarán también protagonistas y representantes institucionales, entre ellos Germán Beardo, alcalde de El Puerto de Santa María y vicepresidente de la Diputación de Cádiz, y Carmelo Navarro, concejal delegado de Impulso Económico, Industria, Logística, Mundo Rural y Marino, Fondos Europeos, Real Plaza de Toros y EDUSI. La emisión continuará después de la llegada de los principales favoritos. Desde la meta de Jerez, Radio MARCA recogerá las primeras reacciones de los protagonistas y analizará cómo queda la clasificación general tras una de las etapas más esperadas de esta edición. Sigue de 15:00 a 19:00 horas el programa especial de Radio MARCA y vive la crono decisiva de La Vuelta desde dentro: desde la salida en El Puerto de Santa María hasta la meta en Jerez de la Frontera.

After being absent from WWE programming for several weeks, Seth Rollins returned Wednesday at an untelevised live event in Quito, Ecuador.

According to F4WOnline's Shounak Chakrabarti , Rollins joined forces with LA Knight and Solo Sikoa to beat The Usos and Jacob Fatu in a six-man tag team match.

articles.title: The Best WWE or AEW Wrestler at Every Age
articles.summary: Professional wrestling used to be a young person's sport, with age 40 being the start of a steady decline. Anything beyond that reflected veterans' reluctance to hang up their boots.
articles.body:
Professional wrestling used to be a young person's sport, with age 40 being the start of a steady decline. Anything beyond that reflected veterans' reluctance to hang up their boots.

That is not the case today, with advancements in self-care giving some of the industry's biggest stars the chance to perform well beyond that, with some even peaking after.

Who are the best wrestlers at every age, based on in-ring quality and historical significance? Find out in this compilation.

List compiled based on ages at the time of publishing on September 10, 2026.

The son of a wrestler, Wayne has been around the industry longer than his age would suggest. A veteran competitor earlier than most lace their first pair of boots, he has the potential to be a foundational piece of AEW's bright future. A former world trios champion and Ring of Honor TV champion, the Seattle native has barely scratched the surface of what the future holds for him inside the squared circle.

Evans has connected with audiences in short order, thanks to his natural charisma, frenetic energy, and bouncy offense. Showcased in the Ladder Match for the Intercontinental Championship at WrestleMania 42 this past April, and in subsequent matches against the likes of Gunther, Jey Uso, Rusev, Ethan Page, and more, he has proven to the industry that he is one of the faces of WWE's future and popular enough to be one of its finest young stars now.

The Prodigy may not be the focal point of the Judgment Day right now, but she has already accumulated a resume that would put to shame most her age. At just 24 years old, the Texas native has had some extraordinary matches in WWE's women's division and is on TV nearly every week alongside Liv Morgan and Raquel Rodriguez. Expect even bigger and brighter things from her when she breaks free from the heel group and returns her focus to championship collecting.

It was not all that long ago that Martin earned rave reviews for his singles run in AEW, where he routinely battled top stars and highlighted himself as one of the bright stars in the promotion during brother Darius' absence due to injury. The company failed to follow up on it and he has wandered aimlessly since, but Martin has more than proven himself as the best at his age, with plenty of potential to be even more for the company if it wishes to revisit that singles run.

The other member of Top Flight has not had nearly the exposure that his brother has, with injuries sidelining him on occasion, but he is still a strong worker, and with a minimum of talent across the WWE main roster and AEW, he earns recognition on this list. The older Martin makes infrequent appearances on AEW TV, but he has been relegated, primarily, to Ring of Honor at this point.

Fletcher is not only the best 27-year-old in WWE and AEW, but he is quickly earning recognition as one of the best wrestlers in the world. A strong, physical, intense worker whose matches with Will Ospreay, Konosuke Takeshita, Kazuchika Okada, and countless others have elevated his star, Fletcher emerged from primarily tag team action to become the biggest breakout singles star AEW has produced over the last two years. That he has proven himself against the biggest and best the company has to offer only sets him up to be a central star for the promotion well into the next decade.

The Ruler has passed every test placed before him and, in short order, has established himself as the star of WWE's future. He defeated Brock Lesnar two out of three times, retired The Beast, and won King of the Ring. He has the aura necessary to thrive at the next level and could conceivably win the World Heavyweight or Undisputed WWE Championship tomorrow and be believable in that spot. He beat out Bron Breakker, his current TV foe, for recognition at age 28, indicative of how quickly he has risen.

There is an incredible amount of talent at age 29 across both WWE and AEW right now, including Lyra Valkyria, Gabe Kidd, Dominik Mysterio, and Kevin Knight. Still, none have the star power or the proven track record of performing at the highest levels in the biggest spots that The Eradicator does. Ripley has competed in the best matches of several years, on the WrestleMania stage, when it matters most. She has won titles, helped to elevate the star power and in-ring quality of the women's division. If she can avoid significant injuries, such as the torn meniscus that currently has her sidelined, there is no reason she cannot be the face of all of WWE before all is said and done.

At age 30, MJF has already proven himself as a centerpiece of a major pro wrestling, headlined a sold-out Wembley Stadium, beaten every major star to walk through AEW, and emerged as one of the most consistently great main event performers in the industry. The undisputed best worker in either company at his age, MJF is well on his way to recognition as one of the best of his generation. The only thing that could prevent him from adding to an already sparkling resume? The allure of Hollywood.

Takeshita's toughest challenge at age 31 was Dragon Lee, who has repeatedly wowed fans in his televised opportunities. Still, The Alpha has pushed ahead of the luchador to earn recognition here, thanks to a hard-hitting style and in-ring charisma that have earned him the attention and adulation of fans. His matches with Kazuchika Okada, Kyle Fletcher, Jon Moxley, and others have confirmed the potential that many have seen in him and set him up for a long and successful career with AEW, if that company can fend off any potential suitors.

Carmelo Hayes has been proving himself as one of the most gifted young stars in professional wrestling since his independent days in the Northeast. Despite his tremendous success in NXT as one of that brand's central figures, it has not translated to the main roster yet, thanks to the start-and-stop booking that has plagued others. No worries, though, because Hayes continues to show up and show out every time he gets the call to appear on TV, securing the support of the fans, all of whom want to see the Massachusetts native get the push befitting his skill set.

Ospreay may be the best wrestler in the world and his victory over Kenny Omega in the main event of All In this year may be the last bit of proof he needed to earn that recognition. One half of a marquee match-up destined to earn Match of the Year recognition, Billy Goat proved why he arrived in AEW with pomp, circumstance, much attention, and high expectations. Thus far, he has lived up to them, even while battling a severe neck injury. How great he must be to so confidently place ahead of Darby Allin and Stephanie Vaquer at year 33.

One of the best big-match wrestlers on the planet, Mone has stared every detractor in the face and proven them wrong. Whether it is in the rings of WWE or as part of the AEW roster, the CEO has repeatedly proven that few shine under the bright lights like her. Look no further than her All In match-up with Willow Nightingale, which someone exceeded even lofty expectations. Even competition from her fellow 34-year-old, Jacob Fatu, was not enough to replace her at this spot.

This was one of the toughest ages to decide, thanks to Strickland's sworn enemy and fellow 35-year-old, "Hangman" Adam Page. Add to that the criminally underutilized Rey Fenix over in WWE, and you have tough competition for Swerve. Had this been two or three years ago, Page probably would have bested him for this spot, but Strickland has repeatedly shown out on the biggest stages, paid off the support of the crowd, won the world title, and elevated his star in some of the best (and most brutal) matches in AEW. Look no further than his extraordinary match with Ospreay from June's Forbidden Door.

Liv Morgan Cast in Psychological Thriller 🎬

Bailey's style does not necessarily appeal to everyone and for those fans, Mark Davis, El Grande Americano, or event Montez Ford would have been better options at this spot. With that said, Speedball has had more recognizably great matches across AEW and in his previous stop, TNA, and has worked with top stars from each company along the way. A high-flyer who can do things at age 36 that younger workers can't, he is finally receiving the spotlight and recognition that had eluded him through much of his career.

Richochet, Rush, and Nick Jackson are tough competition and at any given point, could be considered for this spot over her, but Bayley has spent the last 12 years of her career wrestling historically significant matches against every top star the women's division in WWE has produced. She has won titles, outlasted 29 others in the Royal Rumble, and is currently focused on ensuring the long-term future of the industry through her Lodestone Wrestling initiative. That she can step in the ring and steal the show out from under CM Punk, Roman Reigns, Cody Rhodes, and more on any given night only enhances her greatness.

The Rainmaker shook off a bumpy start to his in-ring career with AEW to remind everyone why he was once the standard-bearer in New Japan Pro-Wrestling. Not quite as great as he ever was, The Rainmaker is still an excellent professional wrestler and has found a personality to go along with it. The victor in another stellar showdown with Konosuke Takeshita and Kyle Fletcher at All In in Wembley Stadium, he continues to turn back the clock, blast his opponents with big lariats, and earn the respect of an audience who watched him grow from young afterthought to future Hall of Famer.

Gunther might be the best wrestler in all of WWE, a punishing force of nature who drives the fight out of his opponents with his devastating chops. When he is not using oppressive and overwhelming strikes on his opposition, he is grounding them, making them exhaust their energy for one last-gasp shot at breaking free of his grasp. Then, he puts them to sleep or forces a tap-out. Ask John Cena and AJ Styles. Though his creative has been questionable at late, Gunther remains an extraordinary in-ring performer, as evidenced back at WrestleMania 42, where he and the next entrant on this list nearly stole the entire weekend.

This may be the most controversial pick of all, if only because of the very vocal portion of the pro wrestling fandom that believes Jon Moxley is the best wrestler of his generation. While those fans are entitled to their opinion, Rollins has demonstrated an ability to employ different styles across his career in WWE and can tell a variety of stories in his work, while Moxley's tend to be rather one-note. Some may prefer that, but in this battle between 40-year-old greats, it is Rollins' broader skill set that nudges him past Moxley for this spot.

The Battle for 41: Cody Rhodes vs. Roman Reigns

Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns are destined to be intertwined for the rest of their careers and the battle for age 41 is no different.

Strictly from a traditional standpoint, Rhodes is the better worker. He can employ a technical style and brawl with the best. He can work the overbooked WWE style and will work a dangerous ladder match to great results when called upon.

There is something to say about Reigns' ability to deliver in those marquee match-ups, when the lights are brightest and the expectations highest.

We have seen it out of him on numerous occasions this year, none bigger or more important than at WrestleMania 42, against CM Punk in their Match of the Year candidate, then again in the main event of SummerSlam, where he enjoyed similar results against Seth Rollins.

Even his Backlash battle with Jacob Fatu was great.

On any given day, the outcome could change, and that is a testament to the greatness of both men. They have been trusted by the powers that be to carry the load at the top of the card for a reason.

For now, though, the Tribal Chief barely gets the nod.

There is a slight recency bias with age 42, thanks to Omega's stunning battle with Will Ospreay at All In. From a consistency standpoint, Sami Zayn is the better option, but one cannot simply disregard a Match of the Year candidate the likes of which Omega had on a grand stage like Wembley Stadium. He turned back the clocks, turned on his heel persona, and delivered a masterclass that put his opponent over in what may end up being a watershed moment for AEW. It was a great performance and proof positive of how great Omega has been at times in his career.

Take Mistico's undeniable ring work, factor in the success of his home promotion, CMLL, and his status as the company's top draw and you have a performer who bumps past Damian Priest and LA Knight for recognition on this list. A dazzling high-flyer with great speed and timing, it is no wonder that Mistico is a favorite to worldwide audiences.

The Motor City Machine Guns arrived in AEW recently, meaning Sabin will have the opportunity to remind fans in on a global stage of why he has long been one of the best in the business. While he may be a step or two slower than he was when he was carrying the X-Division as part of the TNA roster, Sabin is still a more than capable professional wrestler who should acclimate himself with the AEW roster in a way he never really could in his year-long stint with WWE.

This one came down to Balor vs. Claudio Castagnoli of AEW's Death Riders. While the latter is a superb professional wrestler, one would be hard-pressed to argue that he has not taken even the smallest step back, while The Prince appears rejuvenated and ready to make one last, great run in WWE after years of being saddled with The Judgment Day. Still a superb professional wrestler, Balor has recently proven himself against CM Punk with championship gold on the line in two title bouts.

Orton is a worker's worker, a slow, methodical, calculating wrestler with a mind for story beats and understanding of the value of facial expressions and body language. His style is not everyone's cup of tea and can sometimes trend into "boring" territory, but he is very much a throwback to a bygone era. Fans love him and his recent match on Sunday Night's Main Event with Cody Rhodes was a banger until the overbooked finish. He still feels like a Superstar with a banger or two left in him, but Father Time and a serious back injury have certainly slowed The Viper down, even as he remains one of the greatest in WWE history.

The Best in the World has been red-hot this year, delivering some of the finest work of his career at age 47. He has a Match of the Year candidate against Roman Reigns from WrestleMania 42 on his resume, has rejuvenated Finn Balor in two championship clashes, welcomed Kevin Owens back to the squared circle with a superb world title match in Toronto, and reminded the audience of what Johnny Gargano could do in their title bout. A man on a mission to prove his moniker right, Punk was an no-brainer selection at 47.

Emi Sakura continues to compete in AEW occasionally, including a Ring of Honor taping alongside Deonna Purrazzo against Allysin Kay and Marti Belle. Though her appearances in the company are becoming more limited, Sakura is still an immensely talented wrestler and one of the more celebrated Joshi competitors in the world.

Lashley has no business being as dominant physically as he is at 50. Still looking like a god chiseled from granite, the former AEW World Tag Team Champion continues to tear through opponents and prove that he can have success at this point in his career outside of the WWE bubble. With partner Shelton Benjamin, the Hurt Business leader has continued to thrive in AEW, where he has hardly tested himself against the truly tippy-top main event stars.

Mysterio has no business being as good as he is at 51 years old, especially with the plethora of knee injuries he has battled throughout his Hall of Fame career. Yet, he still pops up on Monday Night Raw and in AAA, turning back the clock and having genuinely strong matches. In the argument for a top-five, top-10 at worst, spot in the GOAT discussion, Mysterio was the obvious choice here, even if the competition was the great Shelton Benjamin.

The Rated R Superstar may not be as good as he once was, and he may not have an abundance of time left in the ring, but he has proven he will go out on his own terms while wrestling the best that AEW has to offer. While some of his early stuff was hit-or-miss, his reunion with Christian Cage has bought both of them added time as active competitors and helped provide the company with some genuine dream matches against other all-time-great tag teams.

Truth is as beloved a performer as there is in WWE and although he trends more comedic than anything, he can still go in short bursts. Primarily a tag team wrestler at this point with partner Damian Priest, Truth still brings the energy and pops a crowd like few others. That he has borrowed John Cena's move set in recent years does not hurt.

Rhodes may be sidelined as he recovers from double knee replacement surgery, but The Natural has repeatedly proven that age is but a number. With deceiving quickness and an ability to throw fists with the best of them, Rhodes remains a double-tough wrestler who wears his emotions on his sleeve, an element that oftentimes enhances his work.

A product of the Memphis territory, Jarrett still throws some of the best punches in professional wrestling and has a mind for the business few others on this list can compete with. Still in tremendous shape at 59, Jarrett can hang with some of the brightest young stars in the industry and has proven a knack for playing heel or babyface effectively. One of the greats and a guy history will remember kindly, Jarrett is a treasure and a wrestler who has made the industry better along the way.

Billy Gunn has no business looking a great as he does at 62 or moving like he does when he is called on to compete. Still showing the same pop and speed that he did at his peak, he is an extraordinary athlete who never outkicks his coverage, per se. He knows what he can do, does not venture outside of it, and the results are meaningful performances at this point in his career.

articles.title: ‘Trust has been broken’ – French FA officially withdraws support for Gianni Infantino
articles.summary: The French Football Federation (FFF), through the voice of its president Philippe Diallo, has officially announced that it is withdrawing its support for FIF...
articles.body:
The French Football Federation (FFF), through the voice of its president Philippe Diallo, has officially announced that it is withdrawing its support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino.

Initially convinced by the Italian-Swiss leader's bid to succeed himself ahead of the FIFA presidential election, due to be held on 18th March 2027 in Rabat, Morocco, Diallo explained that "from July onwards, the reasons that led us (the FFF) to support his candidacy have been overturned" and that the conditions for that support "were no longer met" .

These conditions were primarily undermined by Infantino's plan to privatise the World Cup, which, according to the FFF president, was "carried out without any consultation or information" .

Explaining that he had opposed the proposal "both in form and substance" and welcoming the fact that "pressure exerted by several confederations had led to the withdrawal of this proposal" , Diallo stated that the FFF considered "that trust has been broken" .

"The way in which world football is being run no longer reflects our values. That is why, by a unanimous decision of its members, the FFF has decided to withdraw its support for Gianni Infantino's bid for the FIFA presidency. Our position is clear and forms part of a wider movement within UEFA."

"We have a historical right to intervene; France is one of FIFA's founding members. We also have a sporting right to do so: for the past 10 years, France has been one of the top three nations in the FIFA rankings."

Concluding his remarks by explaining that it was not enough simply to criticise, but that proposals must also be put forward, Diallo stated that " at the next UEFA Executive Committee meeting in a few days' time, a framework for our contribution must be established to determine what we want to achieve after early March regarding the leadership of FIFA. And to select the candidate who will represent us in this election."

articles.title: Los Angeles Dodgers to place Shohei Ohtani on injured list, call up top prospect
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers will place Shohei Ohtani on the injured list and call up prospect Josue De Paula, manager Dave Roberts announced Thursday.
articles.body:
Sept. 10 (UPI) -- The Los Angeles Dodgers will place Shohei Ohtani on the injured list and call up top prospect Josue De Paula, manager Dave Roberts told reporters Thursday.

Due to his placement on the 15-day injured list, which is backdated to Monday, Ohtani can't return until Sept. 23. The All-Star designated hitter-pitcher missed six of the Dodgers' previous seven games, including a 14-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday in Los Angeles , due to a right arm injury.

"I think, talking to Shohei, the doctors and the training staff, it's the right thing to do," Roberts said at his postgame news conference at Dodger Stadium. "We tried to kick the can as much as we could."

Roberts said Ohtani would be in the Dodgers' lineup if the playoffs started Thursday. He said he is confident he will be "ready go to" by the end of his stint on the injured list. Roberts said the majority of Ohtani's discomfort is coming from his right bicep when he swings.

Ohtani, who won four MVP awards in the last five seasons, hit .277, with 30 home runs and 80 RBIs through 130 games this season. He owns a 1.79 ERA on the mound, but hasn't pitched since July 3.

De Paula, the No. 6 prospect in baseball, is set to make his MLB debut against the Miami Marlins on Friday in Miami. The 21-year-old outfielder hit .303, with 27 home runs, 104 RBIs and 31 stolen bases through 124 games this season for the Double A Tulsa Drillers.

Roberts said Ohtani will be likely shut down swinging for two or three days to calm his injury.

"With Shohei, it's more, let's take the 15 days, get a reset, get him feeling better and know that we still have a week of baseball games left and build him up all the while during this 15 day stint to get the best of him for the postseason," Roberts said.

The Dodgers (89-57) own MLB's second-best record, trailing only the 91-56 Milwaukee Brewers . They hold an 11-game lead on the San Diego Padres in the National League West with 16 games remaining on their regular season schedule.

The Dodgers will battle the Marlins in a series opener at 7:10 p.m. EDT Friday in Miami. That contest will launch a seven-game road trip, which also features a four-game series with the Cincinnati Reds.

Their final three series of the season will take place in California, with six games against the San Francisco Giants and three against the San Diego Padres.

articles.title: “That’s My Problem”: A’ja Wilson Receives Becky Hammon’s Backing Amid FIBA Decision Debate
articles.summary: A’ja Wilson disappointed many when it was announced that she will not be playing in the FIBA World Cup for Team USA. Wilson is reported to be sitting out the...
articles.body:
A'ja Wilson disappointed many when it was announced that she will not be playing in the FIBA World Cup for Team USA. Wilson is reported to be sitting out the tournament as a result of back issues, which she does not want to worsen.

Not just A'ja Wilson, but Kelsey Plum too was reported to be out of the Team USA roster before the team could travel to Berlin. Plum has been struggling with a leg injury and is currently ruled out of the remainder of the season.

The loss of these two veterans in the team got many fans worried, especially for Wilson's absence. Wilson showed incredible leadership during her previous appearances for Team USA, and fans were worried that without her the team might struggle.

At the same time, there were also many who criticized Wilson for being selfish by not playing for Team USA. Aces coach Becky Hammon was recently asked again about this and she vehemently supported her star player, even going on to state that if a man had made this decision, he would not be criticized the same way.

"A'ja has every right to do what she feels best health wise. And the other thing is, the men do this all the time. Can you name me any of the men's world championship rosters right now? Can you name me any person on there? … If this was a man making this decision, there would be nothing to say. And that's my problem," Becky Hammon said.

Even though Hammon is supporting A'ja Wilson for her decision, there have been many who are continuing to take shots at the Aces star for missing the World Cup. Many fans reason that Wilson is not actually battling a terrible injury right now and that she should be playing for her country.

A'ja Wilson Accused Of Being Jealous By Linda Cohn

A'ja Wilson missing the World Cup is because of injury concerns according to the star and those close to her. However, Linda Cohn has another strange theory. A while ago, the former ESPN reporter stirred the pot saying that Wilson is jealous of Caitlin Clark and does not want to be there at the World Cup since the spotlight will be on the Indy star.

Cohn's remarks did not sit well with the crowd, with many calling her out openly on social media and trolling her. This eventually led to Cohn putting out an explanation, with her claiming that she was just asking questions.

articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers: Pat Murphy sounds off on Brandon Sproat after 4-walk ninth inning vs Cubs
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Chicago Cubs to complete the sweep on Wednesday night. They got off to a hot start thanks to Christian Yelich hitting a th...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Chicago Cubs to complete the sweep on Wednesday night. They got off to a hot start thanks to Christian Yelich hitting a three-run home run in the first inning. Milwaukee also put up three runs in the second after home runs hit by Jackson Chourio and William Contreras .

Indeed, the final regular season matchup between the Brewers and Cubs in 2026 was not even close. Well, until it unnecessarily was.

Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy sounds off on Brandon Sproat

Thanks to the stellar pitching (once again) of Logan Henderson , Milwaukee was in complete control of the game all night long. That is, until the ninth innning.

JJ Romero pitched scoreless frames in the sixth and seventh innings. With the Brewers up 8-1 at that point, manager Pat Murphy decided to bring in Brandon Sproat, who had been called up earlier this week when Grant Anderson went on the injured list.

Sproat pitched a scoreless (but not clean) eighth inning, so Murphy decided to leave him in for the ninth. He promptly walked four consecutive batters, leading to a run. Abner Uribe was brought in with the bases loaded and one out, but could not limit the damage.

In the end, Milwaukee came away with an 8-6 win and a now ten-game lead over Chicago in the National League Central Division. However, Murphy was far from pleased with Sproat's performance.

"It's unacceptable. You got to throw the ball in the plate or you can't be a major league pitcher," he told reporters after the game.

As fans will recall, Sproat started out the year with the Brewers as a member of their starting rotation. However, the same control issues that plagued him on Wednesday night led to his eventual demotion to Triple-A.

When the dust settled at American Family Field, Sproat was tagged for four earned runs in 1.1 innings pitched, raising his season ERA to 5.57. That simply is not good enough for a team that has the best record in baseball and World Series aspirations.

In short, it will be very surprising if Brewers fans see Sproat pitch again for Milwaukee this year. If Murphy cannot even trust him with a seven-run lead, there is no way he should be used in any other situation going forward.

articles.title: 7 Free-Agent Landing Spots for Chris Kreider After Being Waived by Ducks
articles.summary: Business in the NHL picked up in a big way on Wednesday when the Anaheim Ducks placed Chris Kreider on waivers for contract termination. The Ducks need to get RFA Cutter Gauthier re-signed and ending Kreider's contract frees up $6.5 million in cap space to make that happen.
articles.body:
Business in the NHL picked up in a big way on Wednesday when the Anaheim Ducks placed Chris Kreider on waivers for contract termination. The Ducks need to get RFA Cutter Gauthier re-signed and ending Kreider's contract frees up $6.5 million in cap space to make that happen.

Kreider potentially gets the chance to sign somewhere new (if he isn't claimed on waivers, that is) and after he put up 22 goals and 28 assists last season in 75 games and another seven points in 12 playoff games. At 35 years old, he's older but he's still got game and teams in need of a guy who menaces goalies with his presence around the net and ability to score on the power play, he'll be in demand.

There are enough teams who could use a player with Kreider's skill set but, as Elliotte Friedman shared , he would like to go back East to be closer to family. We've picked out a handful of teams who could be players for the former 50-goal scorer and reasons why they'd be in the hunt.

As much as Chris Kreider going back to the Rangers would be a homecoming, if he signed with the Boston Bruins, it would be a true return home for the Boxford, MA native and Boston College alum.

Kreider would give the Bruins a net presence in the mix with guys like David Pastrňák and J-J Peterka who use speed and skill to get pucks on the net and generate offense. Although Kreider wouldn't help Boston by getting faster, he would fit in well with them to make games meaner around the crease and add another weapon to the power play.

Kreider going back to Boston for the first time since he helped Boston College win the 2012 National Championship would be a true sweetheart story and playing for the Bruins, who could use his help to deepen the lineup, makes it a natural fit. Boston has just over $5 million in cap space and that's enough to make them serious contenders if they want to be.

There's been so much intrigue around the Buffalo Sabres this offseason and not just because of their fun run to the second round of the playoffs. They lost Alex Tuch and Bo Byram this summer and while they were able to find a similarly skilled defenseman to replace Byram, they didn't do the same with Tuch. Chris Kreider would come close to doing that.

The Sabres have a bit of a crowded house at forward and adding another veteran like Kreider would make it a bit difficult for all of their younger forwards to stick around (Konsta Helenius, Noah Östlund, Jiri Kulich to name a few). Then again, if the Sabres are still trying to pull goalie Connor Hellebuyck out of Winnipeg in a trade, some of those young players might not be around and thus open the door for Kreider. A move of that magnitude might be the kind of thing that convinced Kreider to go to Buffalo, but a move like that right before training camp opens would be stunning.

Kreider has experience with Sabres coach Lindy Ruff who was an assistant with the Rangers for three years while he was there, so that connection is enough to put the Sabres on the radar. But what Kreider can do at even strength and on the power play are reasons enough for Buffalo to want him regardless.

The Hurricanes have been really quiet this offseason. They've been busy celebrating their Stanley Cup win, of course, but when it comes to making moves, they haven't tinkered with much of anything. Being the defending champions, however, puts them in prime position to add a veteran like Chris Kreider with ease.

The 'Canes don't need to mess around with their lineup much because what they've got works really, really well. But if they added a net bully like Kreider who's got the kind of touch with the stick and ability to ruffle feathers in the crease, it makes him an ideal player for how they pump pucks on the net in the offensive zone.

Kreider's ability to tip pucks and get to rebounds to score goals in the dirty areas make him an attractive player for any team, but with how Carolina fires so many shots, Kreider could make an offensive killing there be it with goals or assists. The Hurricanes don't need the help on the power play (24.9 percent, fourth best in the NHL), but a guy like Kreider could make them even better.

They've got cap space and they're without Seth Jarvis and Eric Robinson to start the season thanks to injuries and Kreider would love to win a Cup.

Trades That Could Happen Before Training Camp

Few Rangers players over the years have been as beloved as Chris Kreider was and when he was moved to Anaheim a year ago, albeit in a somewhat predictable trade, it cut the fans deep to see him no longer in Manhattan. If he wants to head east and return home, the Rangers would undoubtedly have interest.. right?

New York has had a solid offseason and if they were able to woo Kreider back to the Blueshirts, it would give their forward group a lot more depth and someone more than familiar with how things work there. Although he'd be playing for a new coach in Mike Sullivan, Kreider's knack for scoring in big moments for the Rangers on top of his steady production would make the move an instant hit.

There's a pretty big catch, however, as the Rangers are tight to the cap (PuckPedia.com has them just under $1 million under the ceiling). They've also added their own depth with Eeli Tolvanen and have other younger players they'd like to work into the lineup. Then again, a productive Kreider would give the Rangers a lift in more than a few ways. If they can figure out a way to make it work under the cap, it'd give them a lift they weren't expecting to make.

As much as Kreider returning to New York makes sense, what if he went a little bit further east than Manhattan out to Long Island instead? Before Rangers and Isles fans send us insults for the suggestion, the fit makes a lot of sense.

Kreider would give the Islanders a tested veteran scorer on the wing, something they lost and were unable to replace when Anders Lee signed with Utah as a free agent. One look at the Islanders roster tells us they need someone else who can score goals and work on the power play, especially with Matthew Schaefer directing traffic from the blue line.

Kreider's work around the net and ability to agitate any defenseman and goalie in the league with his presence fits the attitude the Isles have played with over the years, and coach Pete DeBoer would undoubtedly love to have a veteran like him to contribute. The Islanders offseason was very quiet and adding a former beloved Ranger to the lineup would be enough to juice up the rivalry again.

The Flyers have spent the summer trying to add more offense to the lineup and tried doing it in a big way by signing Leo Carlsson to an offer sheet that Anaheim matched. It would look like a 4-D chess strategy if the Flyers were able to land Chris Kreider because they helped put the Ducks in a cap bind.

Kreider would give Philly a boost along the wing where they've already got some strong players in Porter Martone, Owen Tippett, Travis Konecny and Matvei Michkov. Kreider's strengths and abilities would make him a natural mentor for Martone while also putting him in position to make sure the Flyers go back to the playoffs.

When you factor in Kreider's ability to contribute to the power play, he's a player that makes a ton of sense for the Flyers given how poorly they fared on the man advantage (15.7 percent, last in the NHL). Anywhere in the northeast is close to home for Kreider and the Flyers have more than enough cap space to work with (more than $13 million) if they need that to help win him over.

One thing we know about the Penguins is that they've got an older team and the one upside to having a group like that is adding one more veteran doesn't really hurt, right? That's why Chris Kreider makes sense.

Kreider's net presence and power play ability would give the Penguins something they could desperately use. Not since Patric Hornqvist have the Pens had a guy more than happy to hang around the front of the net and bother opponents and Kreider's got a fair bit more scoring touch from the circles and slot. The Penguins having defensemen like Kris Letang and Erik Karlsson who can shoot with skill to produce goals of their own or set up deflections would make Kreider an ideal player to make that happen as well.

Kreider teaming up with Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin might make Rangers fans throw-up in their mouths, but with the Penguins eager to have more playoff magic in their star players' waning years, adding Kreider to make them deeper and more dangerous makes sense.
